title: Journey to the West (Xi you ji / 西遊記)
creators: Wu Cheng'en (traditional attribution, not re-verified this session)

access.edition_or_version: Anthony C. Yu's revised translation, University of Chicago Press, 2012 (4 volumes; original translation 1977-1983); bibliographic record verified via Open Library ISBN 9780226971315 on 2026-09-24

mechanics.premise: A monk's scripturally sanctioned pilgrimage to India is escorted by a band of fallen celestial creatures, chief among them a rebellious monkey of immense power.
mechanics.deflation_targets: The celestial bureaucracy itself — heavenly officials, dignitaries, and divine rank repeatedly embarrassed by the monkey's irreverence (from standard plot summary; text not inspected this session).
mechanics.licensed_frame: Folkloric-comic tradition of the pilgrim tale plus the trickster's structural role: mockery is licensed by the monkey's defeat-and-service narrative rather than free-floating.
mechanics.point_of_view: Omniscient classical narration alternating cosmic register with farcical episode.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Episodic trickery; bureaucratic parody of divine hierarchy; register whiplash between scriptural solemnity and street quarrel (described from standard summary only — Tier-5 context, disclosed, never quoted).
mechanics.dialogue: Heavenly officials speak with formal gravity that the monkey's answers deflate.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Adventure-comic: suspense of each trial resolved partly by deflating whoever claims unassailable rank.
mechanics.boundaries_and_restraint: Its deflation of officialdom edges toward satire of real worldly bureaucracy; card use should note the partial, summary-based analysis.
mechanics.conventions: Canonical classical Chinese novel; pilgrimage frame with supernatural escort.
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Makes the highest possible hierarchy (the celestial administration) a legitimate comic object — irreverence at the summit of the world-order.
mechanics.critical_reception: Standard Chinese literary classic; Yu's 4-volume translation is the standard scholarly English version (bibliographic verification only).
mechanics.audience_reception: Foundational across East Asian popular culture (stage, film, television); an SFE entry for Wu Cheng'en was not found (404), recorded as a gap.
